incident-bot: PAGER: [HIGH] model-catalog-service - unexpected default revision for model 'redwood-medium-v2' (pagerduty.com/incident/PD12345) :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 triggered for service 'model-catalog-service'. Urgency: high. Acknowledgement required.

emma: acked on pagerduty. I'll take initial triage. Paging eng-oncall rotation.

raj: on call, joining. what symptoms?

mike: seeing a spike of 500s from catalog read endpoints. quick grep in logs shows catalog entry for redwood-medium-v2 has default_revision set to "rev-20260228-xyz" but that revision was removed in last catalog prune job. requests are failing when resolver tries to pull artifact. Example error: `ArtifactNotFoundError: model artifact not found for rev-20260228-xyz`

laura: customer-facing alert: a few power users reported generation failures (500) around 14:00 UTC. not widespread yet but clearly degradations. Tracking list: alpha-inc, beta-startup.

emma: is this a bad defaults write (operator error) or an automated job?

mike: looks like an automated catalog promotion job set default=false -> true on that revision after a bad ingest. I see a Jenkins job `catalog-promote` ran at 13:58 UTC and returned 0, but the artifact prune job finished 13:55 UTC and removed the artifact. race condition.

chris: can we hot-fix by flipping default to previous known-good revision? which revision was last known good?

mike: yes. last good is rev-20260210-stable. I'll set default to that and update routing to fallback to the stable shard while we investigate.

emma: execute and post commands/results. include outputs.

mike: running admin CLI now:
```
# set default back to stable
redwoodctl catalog set-default --model redwood-medium-v2 --revision rev-20260210-stable --reason "hotfix revert after promotion-prune race"
```

mike: CLI output: `OK: default revision for redwood-medium-v2 set to rev-20260210-stable`

mike: pushing a routing flush to ensure servers pick up new default:
```
redwoodctl infra flush-routing --model redwood-medium-v2
```

mike: flush job queued, patch applied.

laura: monitoring metrics. error-rate on catalog read endpoints dropping from 8% -> 1.2% over 2 minutes. customers reporting improved behavior.

raj: good. any customer-facing followup we need to do? postmortem?

emma: yes. we'll send a brief note to affected customers. include root cause: catalog promotion / prune race. mitigation: reverted default and will patch promotion job to verify artifact existence before marking default.

chris: creating follow-up tasks:
- add pre-promotion artifact existence check (ENG-3421)
- make prune job archive for 10m before hard delete (ENG-3422)
- add canary gating for promotions (ENG-3423)

mike: also adding monitoring alert for promotion-vs-prune conflicts (metric: promotions_with_missing_artifacts).

pagerduty-bot: PD12345 acknowledged by emma at 2026-03-12T14:07:02Z.

emma: handoff note for next oncall (raj taking remainder):
- incident: PD12345 - model-catalog default revision mismatch
- status: mitigated; default set to rev-20260210-stable, routing flushed, error rate returned to baseline
- next actions: monitor for 30m, apply ENG-3421/3422 patches tomorrow, coordinate with release infra to add precheck

raj: got it. I'll monitor and take any follow-ups.

laura: customer notif draft: "We detected a configuration race that temporarily pointed model requests to a removed model revision. We've reverted the catalog default and taken steps to prevent recurrence; we're monitoring and will follow up with a root cause update." anyone want to edit?

chris: short and clear. add estimated affected window: 13:55-14:05 UTC and list example customers.

emma: sending customer note now.

mike: marking incident as resolved in internal tracker after 30m observation if stable. will attach logs + commands in ticket.

pagerduty-bot: PD12345 resolved by emma at 2026-03-12T14:44:49Z (duration 37m).

emma: final: monitoring window passed, no regression observed. closing thread. adding postmortem ownership to chris

chris: thanks all. follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
